short_answer: Tom Stryker is a real, long running seller. His site names a company, Team Stryker Sports, gives a mailing address in Granger, Indiana and a toll free number, and lists prices for every package. His name shows up in betting forums as far back as 2010. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money is a separate question, and nothing we could open answers it. The numbers on sale are runs such as "26-7 ATS" and "19-0 ATS" built into product titles, plus a claim of back to back college football titles at The Sports Monitor. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick.

Treat Tom Stryker as an experienced seller with marketing records, not a proven winner. The bigger packages cost $1,395 to $2,295, all sales are final, and we found no guarantee of any kind, so record every pick yourself before you commit real money.

guarantee: We found no guarantee on any Team Stryker package page. The site terms say "All sales of “Digital Goods” are final," and that the company will not refund a subscription cancelled part way through a billing period.

The Playbook page is headed "Today's Guaranteed Picks" but shows no terms explaining what is guaranteed. A buyer who loses money betting the picks gets nothing back, and betting losses are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: The copy is not kept up to date. The About page counts from 1984 and claims more than four decades, while the BigAl.com bio still says 36 years, and its most recent dated event is from December 2019.

The BigAl.com page claims both a 15 and 2 record on NFL Games of the Year since 2009 and an 11 year streak of cashing them. The football page gives Lee Stryker records over four seasons in one place and six in another. Dollar figures assume a stake per star rating, such as $100 a star, that a buyer may not use.
Every run starts on a date the seller picked. A streak cut from a longer history tells you little; every handicapper has a hot stretch somewhere.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every Tom Stryker pick with the line, the odds and the release time, no Sports Monitor results we could open, and no court or regulator record about the service.

What sellers publish: product titles with ATS runs on teamstryker.com and BigAl.com, and a Playbook page with a "Last 10 Results" heading that showed no numbers when we looked. A reseller account on X, Churchill Syndicate, posted that Stryker went 3 and 0 on 9 Nov 2026 with Detroit, San Francisco and Seattle, but that account sells packages itself, so it is marketing, not an audit.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Tom Stryker is thin. We found no buyer review of a paid package, good or bad. Our Reddit search was partial. The Reddit archive's full text search timed out all day, so we searched our saved copy of r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting posts from January 2024 to November 2026, plus a few smaller betting subreddits and the comments of 329 saved threads. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found six items in all, on three sites, from 2010 to 2026, and none is a review of a paid package. A 2010 Sportsbook Review thread discussed his free college football systems: most replies were curious or encouraging, one questioned whether such systems hold up, and the starter reported a 3, 1 and 1 first week. On TheRX in 2025 and 2026 his plays were reposted with the seller's own ATS runs, and the forum lists his name among services members should not post. The only results posts came from a reseller on X. We found no complaints and no buyer praise of the paid service.

On Sportsbook Review, a member shared three college football systems that Stryker had given out as free tips, with long ATS records, and said he had started betting them. A week later he reported a 3, 1 and 1 week and said he would keep going. That is a tiny sample of free systems, not paid picks.

Replies in the same thread were split. Two members called the systems interesting or solid, one asked where the numbers came from, and one argued that systems with many conditions tend to be less predictive than they look.
In a TheRX service play thread, a member reposted three Stryker plays with the seller's titles, such as a "36-16 ATS" high noon play on Texas. Nobody posted how they did.

TheRX posting rules for its daily service play threads list Tom Stryker, spelled with an extra y, among services members should not post, and again among services whose write ups should not be posted. The rules give no reason.

Churchill Syndicate, an X account that sells packages and links to churchillsports.com, posted that Stryker went 3 and 0 for $3,000 on a Sunday of NFL sides. It is a seller's results post, not a buyer report.

Our saved Reddit copy had no post or comment naming Tom Stryker, and live Reddit archive searches timed out. Web searches found no Covers or Sportsbook Review buyer thread about his paid packages and no Better Business Bureau, court or regulator record. One reseller page about him would not load, so we left it out.

conflicts: Team Stryker sells picks from Big Al McMordie and Rocketman alongside Stryker's own, and BigAl.com sells Stryker's plays. Each site's praise for the other is part of a sales relationship.
The only results posts we found outside his own sites came from Churchill Syndicate, an X account that sells its own packages. That is marketing from another seller, not independent tracking.
strengths: A named company with a mailing address, a toll free number and written terms.
Every package on teamstryker.com shows its price, from $30 single plays to a $2,295 year.
Free daily plays are posted on the site, so a buyer can watch before paying.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a run chosen by the seller.
All sales are final and we found no guarantee, even on packages costing $1,395 to $2,295.
Bios and records disagree from page to page, and some copy is years out of date.
The terms say they are governed by the law of England, although the company address is in Indiana.
His plays are on TheRX's do not post list, which limits outside tracking.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, long running seller with a named company, an Indiana mailing address, a phone number and published prices. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because he does not publish a full record of every pick, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Tom Stryker cost?
On 17 Nov 2026 teamstryker.com sold single plays at $30, a football week at $125, a month at $350, season clubs at $495 to $595 and a one year pass at $2,295. Playbook sold a one day pass at $49.
Does Tom Stryker have a verified record?
No. The sales pages show runs such as 26 and 7 ATS and claim Sports Monitor titles, but we found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

You get a veteran's plays and some free picks to judge first. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and all sales are final, so a losing month costs you the fee as well as your bets.
